quarterly_data.quarter: Dai Nippon Printing results briefing: FY2025 (ending March 31, 2026) Financial Results and New Medium-Term Management Plan (05-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Results for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (DNP's 'FY2025'), Senior Managing Director Kuroyanagi: net sales grew 3.8% and operating profit 7.9%, 'double the growth in net sales', to JPY101 billion; ROE was 8.9%, above the 8% target of the medium-term plan; net profit fell 6.1% because gains on sales of investment securities decreased. By segment: Smart Communication operating profit +JPY5.4 billion (+15.4%) on photo printing materials, BPO and the reorganisation of publishing and marketing; Life & Healthcare +JPY13.5 billion (+56.6%) on raw-material changes, structural reforms and cost cuts in packaging despite sluggish demand for automotive battery pouches; Electronics -JPY6.6 billion (-11.6%) - Digital Interface was hit by the semiconductor memory shortage from the start of Q4, and in Semiconductor sales rose YoY but depreciation increased on large upfront investment in cutting-edge areas such as EUV, nanoimprinting and glass cores. Management (Q&A): operating profit had been revised up to JPY103 billion but came in at JPY101 billion; Electronics was forecast at JPY57 billion at that revision and came in at JPY50.7 billion (-JPY6.3 billion), more than half of the shortfall from lower metal-mask demand as smartphones could not be produced for lack of semiconductor memory.
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales +3.8%; operating profit JPY 101 billion (+7.9%); Electronics operating profit JPY 50.7 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Dai Nippon Printing results briefing: FY2025 (ending March 31, 2026) Financial Results and New Medium-Term Management Plan (05-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Memory-shortage impact on OLED metal masks (management, Q&A): DNP estimates the hit in Q4 of the year ended March 2026 at about two-thirds of JPY6 billion and expects the negative impact to continue in the fiscal year ending March 2027 at 'the upper end of the single-digit billions-of-yen range' - not four times the Q4 figure, because smartphone-development demand for metal masks concentrates in January-March and the most exposed period runs from about January to April. It is considering ways to make up the shortfall and, despite uncertainty over memory trends, is 'making efforts to achieve upside' rather than focusing on downside risk.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 impact about two-thirds of JPY 6 billion; impact in the year ending March 2027 at the upper end of single-digit billions of yen

quarterly_data.quarter: Dai Nippon Printing results briefing: FY2025 (ending March 31, 2026) Financial Results and New Medium-Term Management Plan (05-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Forecast and new medium-term plan (President Kitajima; Senior Managing Director Miyake; management Q&A): operating profit forecast JPY108 billion for the fiscal year ending March 2027 (DNP's 'FY2026'), JPY7 billion above the prior year, with operating profit in all three segments expected to exceed the previous year and ROE planned at 8%; the forecast includes a JPY2 billion negative impact from the Middle East situation, incorporated for Q1 only. Focus businesses are expected to grow mainly in information security, photo imaging and semiconductors. Medium-term plan (April 2026 - March 2029): operating profit of JPY108 billion and JPY120 billion in the years ending March 2027 and March 2028, growing to JPY130 billion in the year ending March 2029 - above the previous record of JPY120.6 billion - with ROE of 9% (8% or more excluding extraordinary gains and losses) that year; the following step targets operating profit of JPY150 billion or more and ROE of 10% in the year ending March 2032. Planned operating-profit growth: Smart Communication 8% a year on average over three years, Electronics a three-year CAGR of 9%. Q&A: the Semiconductors business is the largest contributor to the plan's profit growth; Electronics accounts for JPY14.3 billion of the roughly JPY30 billion net increase, all from focus businesses. Electronics drivers in the years ending March 2028 and 2029 are Digital Interface metal masks and optical films - rising utilisation of the expanded large G8 metal-mask capacity and of wide-width optical-film lines - with semiconductor photomasks also expected to grow steadily.
quarterly_data.figure: Operating profit forecast JPY 108 billion (year ending March 2027); target JPY 130 billion and ROE 9% (year ending March 2029)

quarterly_data.quarter: Dai Nippon Printing results briefing: FY2025 (ending March 31, 2026) Financial Results and New Medium-Term Management Plan (05-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Investment plan (Miyake; Kuroyanagi; management Q&A): capital investment of JPY300 billion over the three years April 2026 - March 2029 - JPY200 billion in focus and growth-potential businesses and JPY100 billion in business infrastructure, with M&A funded separately - plus JPY120 billion of R&D investment and JPY35 billion of human-capital investment. Investment related to Semiconductors will be the largest part of the JPY300 billion and is expected to see the strongest growth. Under the previous plan (April 2023 - March 2026) DNP invested about JPY390 billion, about 70% in growth investments, including capacity increases in Digital Interface and semiconductors. Structural reforms are to add more than JPY26.5 billion to operating profit from the year ending March 2027 onward versus the year ended March 2023 (JPY6.5 billion in the year to March 2025; JPY21.5 billion in the year to March 2026), through reorganisation, closure of manufacturing sites and business integration.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY 300 billion (April 2026 - March 2029); R&D investment JPY 120 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Dai Nippon Printing results briefing: FY2025 (ending March 31, 2026) Financial Results and New Medium-Term Management Plan (05-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductors (management): photomasks are the front-end focus business; President Kitajima said DNP advanced its microfabrication into EUV masks for cutting-edge semiconductors and is 'currently working toward mass production'. Management (Q&A) expects EUV mask mass production to begin around FY2028 (the fiscal year ending March 2029): full-scale production has not yet started, but test masks have already been sold and sales are expected to increase, and sales of existing masks are also expected to rise. Semiconductor back-end - until now mainly lead frames - is a new growth-potential business: a glass-core pilot line was introduced in December 2025 and samples have begun shipping to some customers; at this briefing glass-core capex was not yet included in the capital-investment plan or the sales and profit plan.
quarterly_data.figure: EUV mask mass production expected around FY2028 (fiscal year ending March 2029); EUV test masks already sold

quarterly_data.quarter: Dai Nippon Printing results briefing: FY2025 (ending March 31, 2026) Financial Results and New Medium-Term Management Plan (05-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Other segments (Miyake; management Q&A): Smart Communication - information security and photo imaging are to grow through M&A and expanded production bases for the global market (photo-imaging manufacturing capacity to be expanded; information-security synergies expected with acquired Rubicon and AUSTRIACARD), and digital marketing becomes a growth-potential business. The acquisition of AUSTRIACARD HOLDINGS AG, announced May 13, 2026, is scheduled to close during the fiscal year ending March 2027, so no earnings contribution is expected that year, but it is already included in the projections for the two following years. Life & Healthcare - the HMI business of DNP Hikari Kinzoku (acquired last year) is to expand in Japan and globally; battery pouches have struggled as the EV market declined, but ESS is emerging and orders for ESS and plug-in hybrid applications have started to come in (not yet in the figures; management sees a possible upward revision); the solar-cell-related business is to expand; aseptic filling systems, already top share in Japan, are to expand globally.

quarterly_data.quarter: Dai Nippon Printing results briefing: FY2025 (ending March 31, 2026) Financial Results and New Medium-Term Management Plan (05-15-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Middle East situation (management, Q&A): Life & Healthcare is the most affected segment, mainly packaging, which uses many petroleum-based materials. Higher material prices are passed on with a time lag after they are confirmed, causing a JPY2 billion negative impact across all segments in Q1, with pass-through assumed from Q2 onward. Packaging customers accept increases relatively easily because they want uninterrupted supply, whereas Electronics prices usually decline daily but have recently fluctuated with the supply-demand balance, so passing on increases there may take time; management is concerned customers could cut purchases if increases become excessive, or suspend production because of material shortages or fuel costs.
